newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks rise to records with Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks rise to records with Wall Street.

text.p: A firm Wall Street boosted European share prices on Monday, with London rising to another record high following news of a major merger in the drinks business.
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar stabilised against the yen after a slide in Asian business and firmed against the mark.
Paris led the way among the major share markets, with the CAC-40 index gaining 1.78 percent while Germany was also buoyant, with the DAX index closing at a record high.
Wall Street gave a helping hand, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 32.56 points or 0.45 percent at 7,202.09 after half an hour's trade.
London's response was relatively muted, but a 17.2 point gain on the FTSE to 4,648.1 was enough to push the index past the previous peak of 4,646.0 set last Friday.
The FTSE rose 175 points last week closing at a succession of record highs, having gained 379 points or nine percent since April 15.
The market dipped on Monday morning due to inevitable light profit taking after such a strong bull run, but Wall Street stopped the selling in its tracks.

The talk of the market was a proposed merger of Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc. The deal, worth more than 20 billion pounds ($33 billion), would create the world's seventh biggest food and drinks group.
By mid afternoon Guinness was up 83-1/2 pence at 600, albeit down from a high of 625, while Grand Met was up 78 at 593, after hitting a high of 613.
Before the Wall Street opening, dealers had expressed disappointment that the merger announcement had not lifted the broader market much.
"(The deal) has helped the sector but people are still a bit uneasy and we're seeing a bit of profit taking especially in financials," said one dealer.
The continental markets actually rose more.
In Paris, the CAC-40 was up 46.97 points at 2,680.88 with the star performer drinks and luxury goods company LVMH, which holds 14 percent of Guinness. It jumped 4.35 percent to 1,438 francs.
Traders said LVMH would benefit from a reevaluation of its stake in Guinness and the merger with Grand Met could open up new outlets for LVMH brands.

The Paris market was also buoyed by opinion polls which seemed to reassure investors that the ruling centre-right parties were holding their lead over the Socialists for elections at the end of this month and in June.
The German market recovered from an early dip and the DAX index closed up 12.96 points (0.36 percent) at 3,575.37, breaking the old record of 3,568.28 set on May 6.
German floor trading ends before Wall Street opens, but the U.S. influence was felt in later electronic trading, where the IBIS index was up 1.35 percent.
Deutsche Telekom closed floor trade up 1.24 marks at 41.19 on expectations of an upbeat earnings announcement at its annual news conference on Tuesday.
The shares have gained 47 percent from their issue last November.
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar stabilised at 118.59 yen, up from a low of 117.50 touched in Tokyo.

Japanese authorities, who during the dollar's recent rally expressed worries about the yen's "excessive" weakness, were content to see the dollar fall. But they had not been prepared to see it crumble quite so rapidly as it did on Monday, analysts said.
On the cross rates, the the mark fell below 70 yen, its lowest level in almost a year.
By mid afternoon, the dollar had climed to 1.6978 marks compared with 1.6843 late on Friday.
Earlier, Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said that a further rise in the dollar would cause a problem with prices and the recent drop in the U.S. currency would not hurt German exporters.
STOCK PRICES AT 1415 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 17.2 points at a record 4,648.1.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 46.97 points (1.78 percent) to 2,680.88.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed up 12.96 points (0.36 percent) at 3,575.37,.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6978 marks compared with 1.6843 late in Europe on Friday and 118.59 yen versus 120.08.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $349.75 an ounce after closing at $346.20 in London on Friday. Silver was up three cents at $4.90.
($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
